newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ATLETICO HAVE THREE SENT OFF, LOSE LEADERSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO HAVE THREE SENT OFF, LOSE LEADERSHIP.

text.p: Atletico Paranaense had three players sent off, were beaten for the first time in eleven games and were knocked off the top of the Brazilian championhip on Sunday.
Atletico twice led against Santos before losing 3-2 to a last minute goal by which time Atletico had been reduced to eight men and Santos ten.
But referee Damasio Oliveira was upstaged in the red card stakes by his colleague Lincoln Bicalho who dismissed five players in the game between Vasco da Gama and Criciuma.

Santos and Atletico provided an enthralling first-half, sharing four goals between them, but the game turned sour when Atletico striker Paulo Rink and Santos midfielder Vagner were sent off for fighting early in the second half.
Shortly afterwards, Atletico midfielder Roberto Ramos was dismissed for a violent foul and team-mate Reginaldo followed with 15 minutes later for a second bookable offence.
Santos, with a two-man advantage, went for all-out attack and scored the winner through Alessandro in the last minute.

Vasco finished with nine men and their opponents eight as Bicalho laid down the law. Players dismissed were Joao Luiz and Edmundo for Vasco and Nielsen, Ivair and Luis Carlos Oliveira for relegation-threatened Criciuma.

Cruzeiro beat Sport Recife to go top of the table while Palmeiras pushed Atletico Paranense into third place by beating Atletico Mineiro 2-0. The teams finishing in the top eight of the competition go into the quarter-finals.

Cruzeiro, Palmeiras and Atletico Paranaense are already through. Fourty-seven goals were scored in the 12 games played over the weekend, the most dramatic games being Sao Paulo's 4-3 win away to Bragantino and Botafogo's 5-3 win away to Juventude.
